rules.effect: The FDA label for ibuprofen says the chance of stomach bleeding is higher if you take other drugs containing prescription or nonprescription NSAIDs.
rules.recommendation: The label says to ask a doctor or pharmacist before use if you are taking any other drug containing an NSAID.
rules.source: FDA OTC Drug Facts label (Advil, ibuprofen), stomach bleeding warning: "take other drugs containing prescription or nonprescription NSAIDs [aspirin, ibuprofen, naproxen, or others]"

rules.effect: NSAIDs impair platelet function and irritate the GI lining; combined with warfarin's anticoagulant effect, this increases the risk of serious bleeding.
rules.recommendation: Avoid NSAIDs while on warfarin unless your prescriber has directed otherwise; ask about acetaminophen for pain instead.
rules.source: FDA label, Warfarin Sodium, Section 7 Drug Interactions

rules.effect: SSRIs such as sertraline impair platelet aggregation; combined with an NSAID's GI and antiplatelet effects, this increases the risk of GI bleeding.
rules.recommendation: Talk to your prescriber before regularly combining sertraline with an NSAID; ask about acetaminophen for pain.
rules.source: FDA label, Sertraline Hydrochloride, Section 7 Drug Interactions

rules.effect: Both increase serotonergic activity. Combining them raises the risk of serotonin syndrome: agitation, rapid heart rate, high blood pressure, tremor, sweating, confusion.
rules.recommendation: Avoid combining sertraline with dextromethorphan-containing cough/cold products unless your prescriber has approved it. Seek care promptly for symptoms of serotonin syndrome.
rules.source: FDA label, Sertraline Hydrochloride, Section 7 Drug Interactions (serotonergic drugs)

rules.effect: NSAIDs can reduce the blood-pressure-lowering effect of ACE inhibitors like lisinopril and, especially with regular use, increase the risk of kidney injury.
rules.recommendation: Use NSAIDs sparingly while on lisinopril; if regular use is needed, ask your prescriber about monitoring blood pressure and kidney function.
rules.source: FDA label, Lisinopril, Section 7 Drug Interactions

rules.effect: Alcohol potentiates metformin's effect on lactate metabolism, increasing the risk of lactic acidosis, a rare but serious condition.
rules.recommendation: Avoid excessive or chronic alcohol use while taking metformin.
rules.source: FDA label, Metformin Hydrochloride, Section 5 Warnings and Precautions (Lactic Acidosis)

rules.effect: Chronic or heavy alcohol use combined with acetaminophen increases the risk of severe liver injury.
rules.recommendation: Ask a doctor before use if you have 3 or more alcoholic drinks per day and are taking acetaminophen.
rules.source: FDA OTC Drug Facts label, Acetaminophen, Liver Warning

rules.effect: Both are sedating antihistamines. Combining them increases drowsiness, dizziness, and anticholinergic side effects without added benefit.
rules.recommendation: Use only one sedating antihistamine product at a time.
rules.source: FDA OTC Drug Facts label (diphenhydramine, doxylamine): "do not use with any other product that contains diphenhydramine or doxylamine, even one used on skin"

_README: No source, no entry. Every rule must cite the specific label section it came from. These are documented interactions from FDA labels and pharmacology references, not predictions, and every one is unverified (verified: false) until a human has opened the cited source.
